test: Encoder contribution to test item #3 (supplementary disclosure)
status: not a certification test item - it decomposes one
question: how much of item #3's 0.9490 is the trained encoder?

cascade_only.sut: src/cpe_match_l0l3.cves_for (L0 NVD CPE index + L3 vendor guard)

reading: The encoder answers 392 of the 6633 components the cascade abstains on (5.9%) and is right on 92.5% of them. It moves the headline by -0.0009. So item #3's figure is the string cascade's; the encoder adds recall at the margin without costing precision.

ungated_sweep.note: the same retrieval across gate settings, over the components the cascade abstains on. Trusted openly (min_sim 0.5, no margin) it scores 0.2636 - three wrong answers for every right one. The sweep's precision-optimal cell is min_sim 0.95 / margin 0.05 at 0.9463, recovering 392, and that recovery count is exactly what the shipped SUT recovers: this sweep is HOW the recall-safe gate was chosen, not an alternative to it. The gate's price is visible here - it declines 94% of the components it could have answered in order to hold precision.

component_metrics.evidence_for: masked-LM adaptation to security text. NOT a retrieval metric - a model can adapt its language modelling and still rank products badly, which is what happened.
how often the correct product is ranked first / in the top k. This is the retrieval metric, and it is poor.
fine-tuning made the vuln/patch matching WORSE than the frozen encoder (0.500 -> 0.426) over 34 pairs - too small to conclude from, too clear to omit.
